transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Well, my wife’s the one who thought I should come in. She says I’m not eating enough. I don’t really see it that way, but most days I just have coffee and toast in the morning, and maybe some soup or vegetables later on. Big meals just feel unnecessary to me at my age.
Have you noticed any significant weight loss recently, even if you weren't trying to lose weight? And have you been feeling more tired or lacking energy more than usual?

My doctor did say the number on the scale has gotten too low. I don’t know that I was trying to lose weight, exactly. I just feel like being lighter makes it easier for me to get around the garden and keep up with my walks. As for energy, I suppose I’m not sure it’s much different than usual.
Have you noticed a decreased interest in eating or a loss of appetite, even when you haven’t been trying to lose weight?

I wouldn’t say I’ve lost my appetite exactly. I just don’t feel the need for much food. Like I said, most days coffee and toast is enough in the morning, and later I might have some soup or vegetables. Big meals just seem unnecessary to me now.
Can you tell me how much weight you’ve lost recently, and whether this was something you intended to happen?

I’m not sure exactly how many pounds. My doctor just said the number on the scale has gotten too low. I didn’t really set out to lose weight, no. I just feel like being lighter makes it easier to get around the garden and keep up with my walks.
Can you estimate how much weight you’ve lost without trying, if any?

I can’t really put a number on it. I just know my doctor said my weight has gotten too low. I didn’t mean for it to happen, but I do feel like being lighter makes it easier for me to move around the garden and keep up with my walks.
Can you recall if your weight loss happened suddenly or if it’s been gradual over time?

I think it’s been more gradual, not all at once. I didn’t really notice it happening day to day, but my doctor says the number on the scale has gotten too low. To me, being lighter just makes it easier to get around the garden and keep up with my walks.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions recently, or have you been feeling ill or experiencing symptoms like fever, nausea, or fatigue that might explain the weight loss?
I’m not sure. I haven’t been told I have any new medical condition recently. I don’t think I’ve been feeling ill in a way that would explain it, but I’m not really sure what else to look for.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing pleasure in things you used to enjoy lately?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve been hopeless, exactly. I still do my usual things, but I haven’t paid much attention to whether I’m enjoying them less.
Have you noticed that activities you used to enjoy don’t give you as much pleasure as they used to?
I’m not really sure. I still do my usual things, like getting outside, but I haven’t thought much about whether they feel less enjoyable than before.
Have you noticed that the things you used to enjoy, like gardening or walking, don’t bring you the same sense of pleasure as they used to?
I’m not sure, doctor. I still do those things sometimes, like walking, but I haven’t really noticed whether they feel different or less enjoyable.
Have you noticed that you don’t get as much pleasure or happiness from things you used to enjoy, like gardening or walking?
I don’t really know. I still go for walks and do some of the usual things, but I can’t say I’ve noticed a big change in how much pleasure I get from them.
Can you remember approximately how much weight you have lost without trying, even if it was gradual?

I’m not sure of the exact amount. My doctor just says the number on the scale has gotten too low. I know I’m lighter, but honestly, to me it feels like it makes it easier to get around the garden and keep up with my walks.
Have you noticed that you don’t get as much pleasure or happiness from things you used to enjoy, like gardening or walking?
I don’t think so, not really. I still like getting out for a walk and being in the garden. I can’t say I’ve noticed less happiness from it… it seems about the same to me.

I still can’t really put a number on it. I know my doctor says the scale has gotten too low, but I don’t feel like I was trying to lose weight. To me, being lighter just seems to make it a bit easier to get around the garden and keep up with my walks.
Can you tell me how much weight you’ve lost in pounds, even if it was gradual and not intentional?

I really don’t know the number in pounds. My doctor just keeps saying the scale has gotten too low. I know I’m lighter, but to me it mostly feels like it makes it easier to get around the garden and keep up with my walks.
Can you estimate if you’ve lost 5% or more of your body weight in the past six months, even if it was not something you were trying to do?

I’m not really sure about the percentage. My doctor says the number on the scale has gotten too low, but I don’t think of it that way. To me, being lighter just makes it a bit easier to get around the garden and keep up with my walks.
